title: Modifying Dysfunctional Cognitions to Address Fear of Pain Catastrophizing and Headache-Related Burden in Cluster Headache: A Randomized Controlled Trial
summary:
Migraine is a common neurological disorder that can have a substantial impact on the lives of those affected. Migraine can also cause significant distress beyond the headache attacks themselves. The way in which pain and its possible consequences are perceived and interpreted may play an important role in this regard. In particular, perceiving pain as highly threatening or unbearable may lead to unhelpful thoughts about the course and consequences of migraine attacks, which may contribute to greater disability both during and between attacks.
This study aims to investigate whether a computer-based psychological online intervention that specifically addresses such unhelpful thoughts can help reduce pain catastrophizing and migraine-related burden.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Migraine diagnosis and validated using the ICHD-3 criteria
Exclusion criteria:
Revoking the declartion of consent; drug-/ alcohol consumption; uncorrected visual or hearing impairment; psychotic symptoms; cognitive disorders that negatively affect learning
